facts.raw_span: a 3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with various topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
occasional otitis media
The family history was negative for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts were present on the scalp
Neck, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes showed no abnormalities
Routine blood examinations revealed no pathological findings
Two osteolytic lesions identified on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes
The infiltrate stained positively for CD1A
Ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes: normal
Serum electrophoresis: normal

concepts.why: The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions, osteolytic lesions, and a subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, along with positive CD1A staining, are characteristic of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions and disseminated erythematous papules could be seen in multicentric reticulohistiocytosis, although the lack of characteristic multinucleated giant cells and other systemic symptoms makes this diagnosis less likely.

The presence of osteolytic lesions and a subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei could be seen in histiocytic sarcoma, although the clinical presentation and lack of other aggressive features make this diagnosis less likely.
